discovery: Quantum information processing and quantum simulation with trapped atoms and ions: from the Cirac-Zoller gate proposal to programmable quantum processors

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information science
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how laser-controlled trapped ions could perform universal quantum logic. This gave the first concrete, scalable architecture for a quantum computer. Blatt's experiments made the proposal real: high-fidelity entangling gates, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entanglement, digital quantum simulation and early quantum error correction with ion strings. Cirac and Zoller also founded the program of analog quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the Bose-Hubbard proposal, and developed the theory of quantum networks and repeaters. Their ideas became the blueprint that trapped-ion, neutral-atom and photonic platforms around the world now follow. Together the three turned quantum optics into an engineering discipline for controlling many-body quantum systems. Today's error-corrected logical qubits and programmable quantum simulators come directly from this work, which opened a new field of physics and a new technology.
